To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the Marshallian forces in a region affect contractual safeguards in R&D partnerships; and (2) the Marshallian effects are more pronounced when they are related to knowledge spillovers.

(1) the Marshallian forces at work in the location where R&D activities take place have an impact on contractual safeguards and (2) this effect is stronger for safeguards that protect the execution of the alliance, rather than the alliance termination, and for safeguards that are more formal in nature.

(1) location externalities arising from Marshallian forces affect governance-related externalities, (2) the governance-related externalities arising from the Marshallian forces affect the specification of contractual safeguards in R&D partnerships, and (3) the governance-related Marshallian forces are distinct from productivity-related Marshallian forces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the governance of R&D partnerships and its relation to the Marshallian forces that are at work in a location.

how location characteristics affect contractual governance in alliances, and it contributes to the alliance governance literature by highlighting the role of governance externalities arising from agglomeration.
how location-specific externalities affect the design of governance mechanisms in interfirm R&D alliances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Marshallian forces in a given location have a bearing on the governance of R&D partnerships, but that this effect depends on the type of governance mechanism considered.
the Marshallian forces at work in the location of alliance activities generate governance externalities that affect the design of safeguards governing R&D partnerships.
the Marshallian forces at work in the region where the alliance activities take place have a bearing on the specification of safeguards in contracts that govern R&D alliances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Marshallian forces produce governance externalities that affect the design of safeguards against opportunistic behavior in interfirm R&D collaborations.

Marshallian forces in a location produce governance-related spillovers that affect the design of formal safeguards in R&D partnerships, which, in turn, have implications for the success of R&D alliances.
Marshallian forces produce governance-related external economies that extend beyond productivity externalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Marshallian forces at play in a given location have an impact on governance-related externalities, which are external to the productivity-related agglomeration economies that previous research has focused on.
the governance of R&D partnerships is influenced not only by the productivity-related externalities arising from agglomeration but also by governance-related externalities.
governance externalities are a key determinant of governance choices in R&D alliances, which are often overlooked in the literature.
